We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={y}^{2}+3\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=2y, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}={e}^{2y-1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y=\int {e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y=\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =({y}^{2}+3)(\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2})(2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\int y\,{e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int y\,{e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=y\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}={e}^{2y-1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y=\int {e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y=\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y\,{e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =(y)(\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{y\,{e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{y\,{e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\int y\,{e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}}{2}-(\frac{y\,{e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}}{2}-\frac{y\,{e}^{2y-1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{4}(2{y}^{2}-2y+7)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}({y}^{2}+3){e}^{2y-1}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{e}^{2y-1}}{4}(2{y}^{2}-2y+7)]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(2)-1}}{4}(2(2)^{2}-2(2)+7))-(\frac{{e}^{2(1)-1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+7)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}(8-4+7)-\frac{e}{4}(2-2+7) \\  & =\frac{11{e}^{3}}{4}-\frac{7e}{4} \\  & =\frac{11{e}^{3}-7e}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
